target_model: inputs/Q014_model.py (632 lines) -- first-order carryover / order-contrast model, scalars only
note: Every row was checked with an actual HTTP request from this sandbox on 2026-09-25; status codes are recorded verbatim. Size is the number of bytes actually received, except where size_source says 'documentation'.

sources.name: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 -- registered AB/BA crossover trials in Parkinson disease
sources.format: JSON (ClinicalTrials.gov v2 study schema: protocolSection.designModule, armsInterventionsModule, statusModule)
sources.license: US National Library of Medicine public data, no copyright, no registration required; reuse governed by https://clinicaltrials.gov/policy/terms-of-use (page reachable, HTTP 200 verified)
sources.subjects: 50 records returned, 46 flagged interventionModel=CROSSOVER; enrolment ACTUAL 8-94, median 24 (n_seq in the Q014 calibration trial = 7 and 9, total 16)
sources.measured_why: Design facts (allocation, model, enrolment, stated period/washout text) recorded by registrars; no outcome measurements. Not counted as measured data.
sources.mapping_argument: designModule.designInfo.interventionModel identifies real AB/BA sequences; the free-text armsInterventionsModule gives measured-in-the-field design values for t_w (48 h, 7 d, 14 d, 15+/-2 d, 1 wk, 3 months) and, for NCT00305331, t_p = 4 wk + t_w = 1 wk + t_p = 4 wk, i.e. t_w/t_p = 0.25 -- the dimensionless ratio the Q014 gates actually depend on.
not_constrains: tau (a washout is a DESIGN length, not a memory constant -- N-C)

sources.name: Remifentanil pharmacokinetics (65 patients, 2107 concentration-time points)
sources.size: 124,398 B (0.12 MB, well under the 50 MB cap)
sources.format: CSV, 12 columns, index col rownames; 2107 rows x 12 cols as loaded
sources.license: Upstream R package `nlme` is GPL-2|GPL-3; the Rdatasets project states NO separate per-dataset licence. Strict licence status therefore recorded as UNKNOWN, not guessed. Original measurement: Pinheiro JC & Bates DM (2000), Mixed-Effects Models in S and S-PLUS.
sources.subjects: 65 patients (30 female / 35 male), 20-54 obs/patient, all 65 evaluable for the decay fit
sources.units: Time = min from beginning of infusion; conc = ng/ml; Rate = ug/min; Amt = ug; Age = yr; Ht = cm; Wt = kg (units read from https://rdrr.io/cran/nlme/man/Remifentanil.html, HTTP 200)
sources.coordinate_frame_why: 1-D time series; a spatial frame is undefined and was not fabricated (PREREG IC7).
sources.mapping_argument: PREREG of the model owner states tau must be 'identified from within-subject decay data (log-linear slope = -1/tau)'. This dataset is exactly that: per-patient monotone decay segments give a measured tau with CI.

sources.name: Quinidine pharmacokinetics (136 patients, 1471 records, multi-dose steady state)
sources.format: CSV, 14 columns, 1471 rows x 14 cols as loaded
sources.license: Same upstream situation as REMIFENTANIL-NLME: R package `nlme` GPL-2|GPL-3, no per-dataset licence stated -> recorded UNKNOWN. Units read from https://rdrr.io/cran/nlme/man/Quinidine.html (HTTP 200).
sources.subjects: 136 patients, 2-47 obs/patient; only 2/136 yield a post-peak log-linear decay segment with >=5 points and r^2>=0.5
sources.units: time = hr from study entry; conc = serum mg/L; dose = mg; Age = yr; Height = in.; Weight = kg
sources.mapping_argument: Intended as the second, independent dataset for null N-B. FAILED: the multi-dose steady-state design leaves no clean post-peak decay segment, so it cannot serve as the N-B replicate. Reported, not hidden.

sources.name: Tetracycline single-dose, two formulations (5 subjects x 4 time points x 2 formulations)
sources.format: CSV, 5 columns, 40 rows x 5 cols as loaded
sources.license: R package `nlme` GPL-2|GPL-3, no per-dataset licence -> UNKNOWN. Unit of `conc` NOT verified in this session -> recorded UNKNOWN.
sources.mapping_argument: EXCLUDED from the tau fit: 4 time points per cell is below the preregistered 5-point minimum. Retained in samples/ because it is a measured two-formulation within-subject comparison, i.e. the closest structural analogue in these samples to Q014's A-vs-B non-commutativity gate G0 (a_B != a_A), but 5 subjects cannot constrain it.

sources.name: MIMIC-IV v2.2 (critical-care time series incl. drug infusion records)
sources.size: landing page 73,729 B; the dataset itself is credentialed (multi-GB) and was NOT downloaded
sources.size_source: measured (landing page); dataset size not measured
sources.license: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License + Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement; open MIMIC code under MIT. Gate: PhysioNet account, training course, CITI 'Data or Specimens Only' attestation, signing the DUA.
sources.subjects: ~73,000 ICU stays / ~65,000 patients (documented, not verified here)
sources.mapping_argument: The only public candidate identified whose intrinsic timescale (hours-to-days of drug effect and of ICU-acquired deconditioning) is the same ORDER as Q014's t_p = 90 d, so the dimensionless ratio tau/t_p can actually be O(1). This is the single most valuable NEXT dataset and was not downloadable within the session.

sources.name: Imperial College 35 femur + tibia bone models (geometry)
sources.size: record landing page 83,917 B; meshes not downloaded
sources.format: STL/PLY surface meshes (per the project dataset map in NIGHT_PREAMBLE.md)
sources.license: Zenodo record licence: must be read per record (not verified in this session -> UNKNOWN)
sources.mapping_argument: SCOPED OUT for Q014, deliberately (PREREG §2, FC-D6). Q014's parameter vector is {t_p,t_w,t_o,tau,a_A,a_B,G,sigma_w,n_seq,alpha} -- all scalar or time-valued. A femoral mesh cannot move any of them. Listed so the omission is auditable; it belongs to the biomechanics questions, not to the order/carryover question.

sources.name: Schissler et al. 2023, Front Neurol 14:1197281, Table 2A + Table 4 (the calibration target the model owner already used)
sources.http_status_why: Not re-fetched in this session; the model owner records it as retrieved and read (inputs/Q014_PREREG.md Sec. 4, PMC10476358). Listed for completeness of the constraint map, not re-admitted as a verified source here.
sources.format: published table (means and SEs, not individual data)
sources.license: Frontiers in Neurology = open access, CC-BY
sources.subjects: 16 analysed (n = 7 Exercise->Usual care, n = 9 Usual care->Exercise)
sources.mapping_argument: Arm-level (not individual-level) means/SEs. This is why sigma_w had to be DERIVED as SE*sqrt(n) and why G remains UNKNOWN: no public source provides the individual-level cells needed to identify G separately from a.

unconstrained_parameters.G: UNKNOWN and not obtainable from any public source found in this session. The latent state is only ever observed through the outcome, so G and a are identified only as a product. Any claim of a measured G would be fabrication.
